title: POC scoping: Riverbend Health - Quality Eval Plan
next_steps: Redwood: send SOC2 + security datasheet and privacy FAQs (Alex) by 2026-03-09
Redwood SE: share benchmark template, test harness, and seed prompts (Priya) by 2026-03-12
Riverbend: provide de-identified sample dataset and production traffic profile by 2026-03-10 (Ethan)
Schedule on-prem perf run with Riverbend + Redwood SE week of 2026-03-16
action_items: Priya Singh (Redwood SE): prepare benchmark scripts and share Git repo link by 2026-03-12
Ethan Cole (Riverbend CTO): export 10k de-identified messages and expected outputs by 2026-03-10
Alex Kim (Redwood AE): send pricing/POC SOW and SOC2 docs by 2026-03-09
Ravi Kumar (Riverbend Security): confirm encryption/KMS requirements and SSO details by 2026-03-11
summary: AE + SE scoped a 4-week quality-focused POC: agree success criteria (accuracy & hallucination thresholds), workload sizing, benchmark plan with golden prompts and regression tests, and timeline for on-prem performance run.
topics: Golden prompts and regression test design
transcript: [00:00] Alex Kim: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm alex from redwood. quick intros?
[00:12] Dr. Maya Lopez: maya here, head of data at riverbend. we're running a couple pilots around clinical note summarization and triage routing.
[00:25] Ethan Cole: ethan, cto. main constraints are latency for triage (sub-300ms ideally), and zero PHI leakage - security first.
[00:37] Priya Singh: priya, redwood solutions engineer. i'll lead the benchmark and perf aspects, happy to dig into datasets and scoring.
[00:50] Samantha Reed: samantha, product. primary success is reducing triage time and increase correct routing, plus high quality summaries for clinicians.
[01:05] Alex Kim: awesome. objective today is align on success criteria, what to test, sample sizes, and a realistic timeline for a poc. also check security needs.
[01:22] Ethan Cole: timeline wise we want a 4 week poc, with a quick smoke in week 1, full benchmarks week 2-3 and decision week 4. is that feasible?
[01:38] Priya Singh: yes that's typical. we'll propose an evaluation plan: golden prompts, hold-out regression tests, hallucination checks, and format validation. also latency/cost benchmarks.
[01:55] Dr. Maya Lopez: for accuracy we want clinical summary F1 > 0.85 on our golden set, and hallucination rate under 2% on critical facts. is that something we can measure automatically?

[02:12] Priya Singh: yes - we'll instrument checks: entity-level fact checks, citation presence if required, and a hallucination detector heuristic. we'll output a per-response score and aggregate metrics.

[02:28] Alex Kim: to be clear on service modes: you asked about on-prem vs hosted earlier. we can run this as Redwood Hosted for initial eval or Redwood Private on your VPC. for perf runs we typically do a dedicated node bench or on-prem harness to replicate network. any preference?
[02:50] Ethan Cole: we prefer private/VPC for data residency and security. we can open a network path for a limited time for bench runs or host an on-prem agent, whatever's easier.

[03:05] Priya Singh: okay we'll plan for VPC-onboarding. for benchmarking we'll need a representative traffic profile: concurrent active sessions, p95 token length, and average throughput (rps). what do you expect?
[03:22] Samantha Reed: production peak is ~80 rps for triage during daytime, with p95 response length around 1.2k tokens. summaries are smaller ~200-400 tokens. we can provide logs for a week.

[03:40] Priya Singh: good. recommended bench sizing: run synthetic load at 100rps steady and 150rps burst, plus a latency SLO of 300ms p95 for triage route. for summaries we set p95 under 1s. we'll include cost per 1k tokens estimates.
[03:58] Ethan Cole: cost estimates are important. also what about quantized models / dedicated GPUs? we might want to balance latency and cost with a 4-bit quantized model if accuracy holds.

[04:13] Priya Singh: noted. part of the eval is model variant testing: open quantized variants and float32 baseline. Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization profiles, but we'll run A/B to measure accuracy regression.
[04:30] Dr. Maya Lopez: on the quality plan—describe the golden prompts and regression suite you propose.

[04:40] Priya Singh: we'll create a golden set of ~500 examples curated by your clinicians that cover edge cases: negation, meds, allergies, temporality. golden prompts will be canonical instruction templates that you want the model to follow.

[04:58] Priya Singh: regression suite: hold-out 2k examples from your production logs, with automated checks for formatting, hallucination, and key-entity preservation. we'll run nightly regression during the POC and report deltas.
[05:15] Samantha Reed: how do you check hallucinations? automated detectors are noisy.

[05:21] Priya Singh: true. approach: heuristic entity overlap and external knowledge checks where possible, plus human sampling. we'll flag high-risk hallucinations (medications, dosages) and run manual review on a stratified sample (5-10%).
[05:36] Dr. Maya Lopez: and scoring? what metrics and weights do you recommend?

[05:40] Priya Singh: propose composite score: 40% clinical accuracy (entity F1), 25% hallucination rate (lower is better), 15% format/adherence, 10% latency, 10% cost per 1k tokens. thresholds: pass if composite >= 0.8 and hallucination <2% and latency within agreed SLOs.
[06:02] Alex Kim: ok that's a good starting point. we'll allow you to tweak weights but want explicit pass/fail criteria.
[06:10] Ethan Cole: can you provide the benchmark harness and result dashboard?
[06:14] Priya Singh: yes, we'll share a reusable benchmark repo with scripts to run locally or in your VPC; results upload to a simple dashboard. we'll also provide CSV exports for your analytics.

[06:26] Samantha Reed: about golden prompts: we want canonical prompts for clinician-facing summaries and separate templates for triage routing with deterministic structured output (JSON with fields).

[06:40] Priya Singh: we'll create both. format checks will validate JSON schema and field presence. when the model suggests freeform text we run additional NER checks to ensure no hallucinated entity insertion.
[06:54] Ravi Kumar: security question - KMS and audit logging; must integrate with our HSM and we need audit trails for all inference requests. can redwood support that in private deployment?

[07:07] Alex Kim: yes - Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and audit logs. for the POC we'll provide limited retention logs and can enable an HSM integration if needed. we'll send SOC2 + architecture docs.
[07:22] Ethan Cole: also SSO/SAML and RBAC for who can view results and config during the POC.
[07:28] Jordan Alvarez: we'll include SSO support and granular RBAC in the private control plane; we'll share setup steps in the onboarding doc.
[07:38] Dr. Maya Lopez: great. anything else on eval? what about human-in-the-loop labeling for edge cases?

[07:45] Priya Singh: yes we'll set up a small manual review loop: reviewers tag hallucination and format failures. those tags feed the regression set for future runs. aim for a stratified sample of 200 items/week.
[08:00] Samantha Reed: what about error budgeting and fallbacks? if model fails format, we want deterministic fallbacks to older ruleset.

[08:08] Priya Singh: we'll recommend fallback policies: for critical routes, if model confidence low or format invalid, fallback to deterministic rules or queue to human reviewer. Redwood routing supports canary/auto-fallback.
[08:24] Ethan Cole: can you show examples of the scoring output?
[08:27] Priya Singh: yes i'll attach sample CSV and dashboard mockup; columns include request_id, route, tokens_in/out, latency_ms, entity_f1, hallucination_flag, format_ok, overall_score.

[08:42] Alex Kim: timeline recap: Week 0 (this week) - agree scope and sign SOW; Week 1 - onboarding and smoke tests; Weeks 2-3 - full benchmarks and nightly regressions; Week 4 - review and decision. everyone ok?
[08:58] Ethan Cole: yes, that aligns. we'll aim to have dataset by mid next week.
[09:06] Dr. Maya Lopez: one more: do you support reranking or chain-of-thought suppression for hallucination reduction?
[09:13] Priya Singh: we support function/tool calling and reranking; we can test output-constrained and chain suppressant prompts. might also test temperature and top-k/top-p tuning.
[09:28] Samantha Reed: about golden prompts: will you lock them during the test so we compare apples-to-apples?
[09:33] Priya Singh: yes — we'll freeze a golden prompt set for baseline runs; additional prompt tuning will be a separate experiment and recorded as a variant.
[09:44] Ravi Kumar: security checklist: encryption at rest/in transit, KMS integration, audit logs, SSO - please provide docs.
[09:51] Alex Kim: will do, sending SOC2 and security deck after this call.
[09:57] Priya Singh: last bit - reporting cadence: we'll deliver a mid-poc snapshot after week 2 and final report end of week 4 including metrics, sample failures, and recommended next steps.
[10:09] Samantha Reed: ok perfect. any blockers?
[10:13] Ethan Cole: none besides getting the sample dataset and legal sign-off on data sharing for de-identified logs.
[10:20] Alex Kim: we'll prepare a minimal DPA addendum for the POC and coordinate with your legal team. i'll follow up.

[10:28] Dr. Maya Lopez: thanks everyone. to summarize: deliverables are security docs, benchmark repo + golden prompts, sample dataset from riverbend, and schedule for on-prem perf run. we'll reconvene after week 2 snapshot.
[10:46] Alex Kim: thanks all — we'll send meeting notes and action items. priya will share the benchmark template. thanks, bye.
[11:00] [call ended]
